answer: Continuous bandwidth-egress attestation caps how many identities one uplink can host: each active node must saturate a dedicated 64 Mbps full-duplex channel with verifiable ChaCha20 nonce streams audited every 30 seconds, where delivery below 95% forfeits the 500 POA epoch bond. Without link-layer proofs, one server can cultivate a vast garden of sockpuppets at zero marginal cost. Under sustained egress checks, whether an operator's bursty relay races like a comet or stalls in a heavy gale, link capacity `C` bounds Sybil count to `N <= C / 64 Mbps`.
